callout.title: Kamikochi as a guided day tour
callout.body: Kyoto connects straight to Tokyo (direct Shinkansen), and Kamikochi is a single guided day tour booked from Tokyo (train + bus + conductor, all handled by the tour operator). No separate hotel, no self-navigated transfers, no reservations to juggle yourself.

legs.detail: JR Kyoto Line, Hankyu, or Keihan all work — Hankyu from Umeda into central Kyoto (Kawaramachi) is often most convenient for sightseeing. Covered by a regional IC card, no reservation needed.

Direct Nozomi or Hikari Shinkansen, no transfers, departures every 10–15 minutes. Reserved seats recommended in peak season but not required — this is about as easy as long-distance travel in Japan gets.

Multiple operators (Viator, KKday, Klook) run this: meet at Shinjuku ~7:00–7:30am, JR Limited Express Azusa (reserved seats included) to Matsumoto, then a chartered bus into Kamikochi. You get roughly 4–5 hours of free time at Kamikochi before the same process in reverse, typically back in Tokyo by early evening. Price is usually around ¥12,000–18,000 per person, all transport and a conductor included — no separate tickets or reservations to manage yourself.
legs.flag: Book this well ahead of your trip, especially for early-mid October — autumn color season is peak demand for these tours.

legs.detail: Direct highway bus from Shinjuku to Kawaguchiko Station (~2 hrs) is simplest. Alternatively, train via Ōtsuki to Kawaguchiko. Buses can fill up on weekends — booking a day or two ahead is safer.
Same route in reverse: direct highway bus from Kawaguchiko Station to Shinjuku (~2 hrs), then local transfer to Ueno. Or train via Ōtsuki.

The Nankai Rapi:t limited express runs direct from KIX to Namba, all-reserved seats, about every 30 min, roughly ¥1,400–1,700 one-way. Cheaper alternative: the Nankai Airport Express (unreserved) takes ~50 min for about ¥970. A Limousine Bus also runs (~70 min, ~¥1,400) if you'd rather skip trains after a long flight.
legs.flag: Landing 7:15pm means you'll likely be on a fairly late train — the Rapi:t runs into the evening, but confirm the last departure time doesn't leave you stranded if your KIX flight is delayed.

legs.detail: The Keisei Skyliner runs direct from Keisei Ueno Station to Narita, non-stop, about every 20 min, roughly ¥2,300–2,600 one-way (cheaper booked online in advance). Cheaper/slower option: the local Keisei Main Line, ~75 min for about ¥1,050. Keisei Ueno Station is a ~2 min walk from JR Ueno Station.
legs.detail_extra: For an 11:15am flight, catching a Skyliner by ~8:30am gets you to Narita by ~9:15am — comfortable buffer for international check-in and security.

tips.title: Should you get a JR Pass?
tips.body: Worth pricing out — the route is now just Osaka–Kyoto and Kyoto–Tokyo, both standard Shinkansen legs. The Kamikochi tour is a self-contained package with its own transport included, so it doesn't factor into the JR Pass math either way. Compare a national pass against buying the two Shinkansen legs separately.

tips.title: IC card (Suica/Pasmo/ICOCA)
tips.body: You only need ONE — Suica, Pasmo, and ICOCA are all interoperable nationwide. Since you land at KIX first, ICOCA is the natural pick, bought right at the airport. iPhone users: even easier — download "Welcome Suica Mobile" from the App Store, set a secret keyword (no account needed), and it's instantly added to Apple Wallet. No purchase to add the card itself, you just top up whatever amount you want via Apple Pay (Mastercard/Amex work more reliably than Visa for pre-arrival top-ups). Covers city trains, subways, buses, and konbini purchases everywhere on this trip — but NOT the long-distance reserved-seat legs: Kyoto→Tokyo Shinkansen, the Kamikochi tour, the Kawaguchiko highway bus, the Sagano Romantic Train, the Hozugawa boat ride, or the Keisei Skyliner. Those all need separate tickets regardless of which IC card you have.

tips.title: Book the tight ones early
tips.body: The Kamikochi day tour is the one to lock in early — these fill up fast during autumn color season, and going through an operator means you're at the mercy of their availability, not just a train schedule.

tips.title: Weather in early-mid October
tips.body: Osaka/Kyoto/Nara/Tokyo are still fairly mild in early-mid October. Kamikochi is a different story — it sits at altitude in the Japan Alps and gets noticeably cold, especially mornings and evenings. Pack real layers just for that one day.

tips.title: Luggage between cities
tips.body: With this many hotel changes, look into a takkyubin (luggage forwarding) service — drop a bag at your hotel in the morning and it arrives at your next hotel next day. Very common and cheap in Japan.
